newsitem.title: USA: Sherwood settles price rigging charges - WSJ.
newsitem.headline: Sherwood settles price rigging charges - WSJ.

text.p: Sherwood Securities Corp agreed to pay $9.2 million to settle civil allegations of improper trading practices, the first Nasdaq Stock Market dealer to do so in a closely-watched lawsuit, the Wall Street Journal said in Thursday's electronic edition.
The proposed settlement still required the approval of U.S. District Judge Robert Sweet in New York City, the newspaper said.

The lawsuit was filed in May 1994 and got class action status in November, the paper said. Lawyers for investors alleged more than 30 Nasdaq market-makers agreed to maintain a large spread between prices they bought and sold Nasdaq stocks, the newspaper said.

Arthur Kaplan of Fine Kaplan & Black in Philadelphia, one of the class counsel, was quoted in the paper as saying at the hearing: "We are in the process of negotiating with several other defendants" in the lawsuit. Lawyers for several other firms declined to comment in the report.
Sherwood Securities is a unit of Sherwood Group.
